title_en: Reinforcement Learning Can Be Recovered From Its Own Rollouts
title_zh: 强化学习可以从其自身的 rollout 中恢复
summary_en: The paper investigates how much knowledge from reinforcement learning (RL) post-training is retained in the rollouts themselves. Replaying the original RL algorithm on archived rollouts causes catastrophic collapse, but maximum likelihood on the archived rollouts (in generation order, without distinguishing correct/incorrect responses) recovers online RL performance. A single maximum likelihood update per rollout batch closely tracks the entire learning curve of online RL. Maximum likelihood on rollouts from the last few RL steps often suffices to recover the final model's performance, suggesting much RL compute goes into discovering an improved sampling distribution rather than learning from samples.
summary_zh: 本文研究了强化学习（RL）后训练中，模型生成的 rollout 本身保留了多少知识。直接在存档的 rollout 上重放原始 RL 算法会导致灾难性崩溃，但按生成顺序对存档 rollout 进行最大似然估计（不区分正确/错误响应）足以恢复在线 RL 的性能。每个 rollout 批次进行一次最大似然更新即可紧密跟踪在线 RL 的整个学习曲线。此外，仅对最后几个 RL 步骤的 rollout 进行最大似然估计通常就能恢复最终模型的性能，这表明 RL 的大部分计算用于发现改进的采样分布，而非从样本中学习。
content_en: Broadly speaking, reinforcement learning (RL) post-training converts compute into model capabilities by training on model-generated data. Typically, the rollouts are discarded after each update, and the knowledge acquired during RL resides in the model weights. In this work, we investigate how much of this knowledge is retained in the rollouts themselves. A natural first attempt is to replay the original RL algorithm on archived rather than freshly generated rollouts, but this leads to catastrophic collapse. We provide a simple explanation for this phenomenon, which in turn suggests a remedy: maximum likelihood on the archived rollouts. Surprisingly, starting from the same base model and replaying the rollouts in the order in which they were generated, without any distinction between correct and incorrect responses, is sufficient to recover the performance of online RL. In fact, a single maximum likelihood update per rollout batch closely tracks the entire learning curve of online RL. Furthermore, maximum likelihood on the rollouts of the last few RL steps often suffices to recover the final model's performance. This suggests that much of the compute invested in RL goes into discovering an improved sampling distribution rather than learning it from samples.
content_zh: 总的来说，强化学习（RL）后训练通过对模型生成的数据进行训练，将算力转化为模型能力。通常，每次更新后 rollout 会被丢弃，而 RL 过程中获得的知识则驻留在模型权重中。在本工作中，我们研究了这些知识有多少保留在 rollout 本身之中。一个自然的初步尝试是在归档的 rollout 而非新生成的 rollout 上重放原始 RL 算法，但这会导致灾难性的崩溃。我们为这一现象提供了一个简单的解释，进而提出了一种补救措施：对归档的 rollout 做最大似然。令人惊讶的是，从相同的基座模型出发，按照 rollout 生成的顺序重放它们，且不区分正确与错误响应，就足以恢复在线 RL 的性能。事实上，每个 rollout 批次做一次最大似然更新就能紧密跟踪在线 RL 的整个学习曲线。此外，对最后几个 RL 步骤的 rollout 做最大似然往往就足以恢复最终模型的性能。这表明，投入 RL 的大部分算力用于发现一个改进的采样分布，而非从样本中学习它。
